name: net_silent_link_reconnects
description: A link that goes silent without a close (Wi-Fi lost, a stalled router or hotspot): nothing gets through either way and TCP reports nothing, which on a real network may take minutes. The game notices on its own: in a match the server speaks every turn, so once its link has brought nothing for away_ms (5 s, as long as the server waits before it calls the seat AWAY) the game drops it and reconnects as from a lost link. Within about 5 s of the mute the overlay says reconnecting and orders are refused; the resume HELLO on a new link takes the seat back, and the hashes agree. Before that, the game's own 7 s stall (it neither reads nor steps) is not taken for the server's silence: what came meanwhile is read first.

steps.assert: not scene.client(2).reconnecting and scene.client(2).reconnect_attempts == 0 and scene.client(2).link.is_open()
steps.msg: its own 7 s stall is not the server's silence: the link is kept
within about 5 s of the silence the game takes the link for lost

steps.assert: scene.client(2).cmd('BUILD', 0, 8, 3) == -1 and scene.client(2).source.closed_note == 'Reconnecting to the server'
steps.msg: orders are refused, and say why
meanwhile the server called the seat AWAY
a resume HELLO on a new link took the seat back
the hashes agree from the rejoin on
